notes: The B variant of daylight-cabin-chase (Colby, typed 2026-09-08 22:19): the same chase from a steep 65-degree high angle instead of straight down, so the figures are larger and the explorer's lounging reads. Probed at 480p as A/B evidence against the top-down; rendered at 1080p only if Colby prefers it or the top-down probe fails.

render.prompt: Locked-off steep high-angle bird's-eye view looking down on the cabin at about 65 degrees, static camera, no push, no zoom, no pan, one continuous twelve-second take. Start exactly from the first frame and continue the same continuous take without any cut. The log cabin stands in the centre of the frame in its clearing of dry golden grass, tall pines around the clearing, a worn dirt path running all the way round the cabin close to its walls; the explorer in the khaki safari jacket and pith helmet reclines on the roof ridge with his tin mug, and on the path below at the cabin's bottom-left corner the young man in the lime-green bucket hat (soft, round-shouldered, heavy-set, washed-out grey hoodie, giant black headphones round his neck, baggy black cargo shorts, long white tube socks in black slides, one matte black can with a green stripe in his hand) is mid-sprint with a huge brown grizzly bear two strides behind him. The young man sprints clockwise round and round the cabin along the path, hugging the walls, and the bear charges two strides behind him at the same pace all the way, so the pair round every corner and pass along every wall in turn and complete about two full laps by the end of the take. The explorer never leaves his spot on the roof ridge: he reclines, sips from the tin mug, turns his head lazily to watch them go round below him, and raises the mug in a small toast as they pass. Sound: two sets of running footsteps circling the cabin, panicked gasping breath, the bear's grunting and one roar, birds in the pines, a quiet slurp from the mug. Live-action documentary realism, shot on a full-frame cinema camera, natural skin and fabric, real dust and pollen in the light, subtle lens flare from the low sun, fine film grain, true-to-life colour. Late golden hour, the low sun raking across the clearing from the west, long warm shadows of the cabin and the trees across the golden grass, warm rim light on the treetops. Physics: feet stay on the ground, the runner keeps the can in his hand, nothing passes through anything, nothing floats, nothing changes size, there is exactly one of each prop, exactly one man on the roof, one runner and one bear, and nobody leaves the path or the roof. No text, no logos.
